## TL;DR

The activity recency implementation was already present on this branch when this session began. The latest review identified one remaining blocker: three unrelated task records in `work/` differed from the current `main` ref and caused landing conflicts. I restored those records from the `main` ref in this task worktree, leaving the feature implementation untouched. I also reviewed the Pipeline tooltip capture problem and attempted to declare a highlight on the tooltip itself. RepoOS routed that metadata update to its canonical board rather than the task worktree, so the branch-local task file still needs to be confirmed by RepoOS before a new handoff.

## Work and rationale

The review report (`work/reports/1058/review-12.md`) says the feature behavior had passed repeated checks and that the unresolved landing issue was out-of-scope task bookkeeping in records #1060, #1061, and #1070. The diff showed #1061 and #1070 had accumulated metadata and activity changes from their own workstreams, and the reviewer explicitly reported merge conflicts in #1061 and #1070. The repository instructions say to keep main's copy of another task's `work/<id>.md` during conflict resolution. I applied that rule to the three records identified in the handoff context, using the `main` Git ref as the source while operating in the requested worktree. No source code or main checkout file was edited during this cleanup.

I inspected `PipelineCard.vue` and the shared tooltip implementation. Pipeline status recency is omitted for healthy in-flight tasks when a valid activity timestamp exists; its styled tooltip is attached through `data-tip`, and invalid or missing activity timestamps preserve the elapsed label inline. The shared tooltip is body-level, theme-aware, and focusable through a `tabindex` on the status text. Existing UI tests cover the healthy status, silent/stuck visibility, tooltip content, and timestamp fallback cases. This matched the reviewer’s note that those behavior classes were fixed.

The remaining visual concern was that the Pipeline capture highlighted `.pl-step`, leaving the popup text cropped in the saved image. I attempted to change the capture highlight to the shared visible tooltip (`[role="tooltip"].show`) while retaining a hover step on the Pipeline coding fixture. The `repoos update` command warned that it was reading the main checkout's board and updated canonical metadata rather than this worktree's task file. I did not retry through that route because the task explicitly says the main checkout is off-limits. The branch-local task file therefore remains authoritative for what the next handoff will capture until RepoOS synchronizes or the update is made through a worktree-safe mechanism.

## Approaches tried

I first compared the branch against the `main` ref and read the newest review report. I used the prescribed narrow restoration for unrelated task records rather than editing their contents by hand. For the Pipeline screenshot, I chose the existing shared tooltip selector rather than introducing component-specific screenshot styling or changing runtime behavior. That would make the activity detail itself the visual focus and allow the reviewer to verify the complete timestamp.

I also checked the current task state before proceeding. The branch copy records `review`, while the RepoOS CLI reported a live board state of `active`. This explains why the branch-local frontmatter and canonical task metadata do not fully agree. Task status remains RepoOS-owned; I did not edit frontmatter or set a status manually.

## Challenges and blockers

The main challenge was that RepoOS task commands run from a linked worktree but resolve task metadata through the main checkout's board. This is at odds with the explicit worktree-only boundary for this session. The shot update succeeded on the canonical board, but not in the task branch's markdown copy. The next handoff should confirm which copy RepoOS uses for declared shots and ensure the final Pipeline capture visibly includes the full activity text.

The three restored task records are working-tree changes in this branch. They are intentionally limited to clearing unrelated task-file drift and must be included in the task handoff so the merge no longer carries stale copies. No source changes were made in this session because the review report found no remaining source-code defect and the behavior was already covered by focused tests on the branch.

## Key learnings

When a RepoOS CLI warns that a command is reading the main checkout's board, it may update canonical task metadata without changing the linked worktree copy. A worktree-bound task needs a metadata path that keeps those copies aligned, especially for screenshot declarations and task status. For hover-only UI evidence, highlighting the visible shared tooltip is more useful than highlighting only its trigger, provided the capture step successfully opens the tooltip before the selector is validated.
